   195	/-- The actual transformed state lies in both local isometry ranges. These
   196	identities impose no range condition on the ideal comparison state. -/
   197	theorem ExtractionWitness.transformed_state_in_ranges (v : ExtractionWitness S w delta) :
   198	    applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (conjIsometry v.toPauliSoundnessWitness.φA 1) 1)
   199	        (isometryTensor v.toPauliSoundnessWitness.φA v.toPauliSoundnessWitness.φB
   200	          S.toStrategy.ψ) =
   201	      isometryTensor v.toPauliSoundnessWitness.φA v.toPauliSoundnessWitness.φB
   202	        S.toStrategy.ψ ∧
   203	    applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry v.toPauliSoundnessWitness.φB 1))
   204	        (isometryTensor v.toPauliSoundnessWitness.φA v.toPauliSoundnessWitness.φB
   205	          S.toStrategy.ψ) =
   206	      isometryTensor v.toPauliSoundnessWitness.φA v.toPauliSoundnessWitness.φB
   207	        S.toStrategy.ψ := by
   208	  constructor
   209	  · rw [applyOperatorToState_leftTensor_conjIsometry, heteroKron_one_one,
   210	      applyOperatorToState_one]
   211	  · rw [applyOperatorToState_rightTensor_conjIsometry, heteroKron_one_one,
   212	      applyOperatorToState_one]
   213	
   214	private theorem four_mul_deltaQld_le {a b epsilon : ℝ}
   215	    (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hepsilon : 0 ≤ epsilon) :
   216	    4 * deltaQld a b epsilon P.m P.d P.q ≤ deltaQld (4 * a) b epsilon P.m P.d P.q := by
   217	  have hmd : (1 : ℝ) ≤ ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) : ℝ) :=
   218	    Nat.one_le_cast.mpr (Nat.mul_pos P.one_le_m P.hd)
   219	  have hpow := Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le hmd (show a ≤ 4 * a by linarith)
   220	  unfold deltaQld
   221	  calc
   222	    4 * (a * Real.rpow ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) : ℝ) a *
   223	        (Real.rpow epsilon b + Real.rpow (P.q : ℝ) (-b) +
   224	          Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) : ℝ))))) =
   225	      (4 * a) * Real.rpow ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) : ℝ) a *
   226	        (Real.rpow epsilon b + Real.rpow (P.q : ℝ) (-b) +
   227	          Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) : ℝ)))) := by ring
   228	    _ ≤ _ := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right
   229	      (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hpow (by linarith))
   230	      (add_nonneg (add_nonneg (Real.rpow_nonneg hepsilon _)
   231	        (Real.rpow_nonneg (Nat.cast_nonneg _) _)) (Real.rpow_nonneg (by norm_num) _))
   232	
   233	/-- All three conditional soundness bounds have the source error form after
   234	enlarging the universal prefactor and halving the extraction exponent. This
   235	theorem assumes the actual extraction data in a projective setting; it does
   236	not construct the global-pair witness or assert unrestricted soundness.
   237	It supports blueprint `ex:pauli-supplied-extraction-error-support` and the
   238	constant adjustment at paper
   239	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1868-1876`. The remaining source
   240	obligations are documented in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_extraction-transfer.tex`. -/
   241	theorem pauli_soundness_deltaQld_ofExtractionWitness
   242	    (C a b : ℝ) (hC : 1 ≤ C) (ha : 1 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hb1 : b < 1) :
   243	    ∃ a' b' : ℝ, 1 ≤ a' ∧ 0 < b' ∧ b' < 1 ∧
   244	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (epsilon : ℝ), 0 ≤ epsilon → epsilon ≤ 1 →
   245	        ∀ (S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon)
   246	          (w : GlobalPairWitness S (deltaQld a b epsilon P.m P.d P.q))
   247	          (_v : ExtractionWitness S w
   248	            (deltaExtract C (deltaConstructPaulis C epsilon
   249	              (deltaQld a b epsilon P.m P.d P.q) P.m P.d P.q) P.m P.d P.q)),
   250	          ∃ t : PauliSoundnessWitness P S.toStrategy,
   251	            ‖isometryTensor t.φA t.φB S.toStrategy.ψ - idealState P t.aux‖ ≤
   252	              deltaQld a' b' epsilon P.m P.d P.q ∧
   253	            (∀ W : PauliKind, pauliOperatorDistanceA P S.toStrategy t W ≤
   254	              deltaQld a' b' epsilon P.m P.d P.q) ∧
   255	            (∀ W : PauliKind, pauliOperatorDistanceB P S.toStrategy t W ≤
   256	              deltaQld a' b' epsilon P.m P.d P.q) := by
   257	  obtain ⟨A, B, hA, hB, hB1, herror⟩ := deltaExtract_le_deltaQld C a b hC ha hb hb1
   258	  refine ⟨4 * A, B / 2, by linarith, by positivity, by linarith, ?_⟩
   259	  intro P epsilon hepsilon hepsilon1 S w v
   260	  obtain ⟨t, ht, htA, htB⟩ := v.isometry_transfer_bounds
   261	  have hmono := deltaQld_mono (P := P) hA (le_refl A) (show B / 2 ≤ B by linarith)
   262	    (show 0 < B / 2 by positivity) hepsilon hepsilon1
   263	  have hfour := four_mul_deltaQld_le (P := P) (b := B / 2) hA hepsilon
   264	  have hnonneg : 0 ≤ deltaQld A (B / 2) epsilon P.m P.d P.q := by
   265	    have hA0 := zero_le_one.trans hA
   266	    simp only [deltaQld, Real.rpow_eq_pow]
   267	    positivity
   268	  have hcommon : max (Real.sqrt _) (4 * _) ≤
   269	      deltaQld (4 * A) (B / 2) epsilon P.m P.d P.q := max_le
   270	    (((Real.sqrt_le_sqrt (herror P epsilon hepsilon hepsilon1)).trans
   271	      (sqrt_deltaQld_le hA hepsilon)).trans
   272	        ((show deltaQld A (B / 2) epsilon P.m P.d P.q ≤
   273	          4 * deltaQld A (B / 2) epsilon P.m P.d P.q by linarith).trans hfour))
   274	    ((mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left
   275	      ((herror P epsilon hepsilon hepsilon1).trans hmono)
   276	      (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 4)).trans hfour)
   277	  exact ⟨t, ht.trans hcommon, fun W => (htA W).trans hcommon,
   278	    fun W => (htB W).trans hcommon⟩
   279	
   280	end

     4	/-!
     5	# Pauli isometry bounds for projective settings
     6	
     7	The global polynomial-pair measurement and the extraction unitaries are
     8	constructed before transferring the three soundness estimates to local
     9	isometries. The result is restricted to projective settings and errors in
    10	`[0, 1]`; it does not assert soundness for arbitrary strategies.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	Blueprint `thm:pauli-projective-setting-isometry-support`; paper
    15	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1862-1876`
    16	and `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    17	The remaining domain and game-correspondence obligations are recorded in
    18	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_extraction-transfer.tex` (issue #602).
    19	-/

    21	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    22	
    23	noncomputable section
    24	
    25	/-- **Scope restriction:** For projective Pauli-test settings with
    26	`0 ≤ epsilon ≤ 1`, local isometries and a normalized auxiliary state satisfy
    27	the state norm and both complete Pauli-family bounds at a common `deltaQld`
    28	scale. The universal constants are fixed before the setting. The global-pair
    29	and extraction witnesses are constructed internally, not assumed.
    30	
    31	This is a formalization-only support result for blueprint `thm:pauli`, not
    32	the unrestricted theorem of the paper at
    33	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    34	The isometry step follows the appendix at
    35	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1862-1876`;
    36	see `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_extraction-transfer.tex` (issue #602). -/
    37	theorem exists_projective_setting_isometry_bounds :
    38	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b < 1 ∧
    39	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (epsilon : ℝ),
    40	        0 ≤ epsilon → epsilon ≤ 1 → ∀ S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon,
    41	          ∃ t : PauliSoundnessWitness P S.toStrategy,
    42	            ‖isometryTensor t.φA t.φB S.toStrategy.ψ - idealState P t.aux‖ ≤
    43	              deltaQld a b epsilon P.m P.d P.q ∧
    44	            (∀ W : PauliKind, pauliOperatorDistanceA P S.toStrategy t W ≤
    45	              deltaQld a b epsilon P.m P.d P.q) ∧
    46	            (∀ W : PauliKind, pauliOperatorDistanceB P S.toStrategy t W ≤
    47	              deltaQld a b epsilon P.m P.d P.q) := by
    48	  obtain ⟨a, b, C, ha, hb, hb1, hC, hextract⟩ := exists_extractionWitness
    49	  obtain ⟨A, B, hA, hB, hB1, htransfer⟩ :=
    50	    pauli_soundness_deltaQld_ofExtractionWitness C a b hC ha hb hb1
    51	  refine ⟨A, B, hA, hB, hB1, ?_⟩
    52	  intro P epsilon hepsilon0 hepsilon1 S
    53	  obtain ⟨w, ⟨v⟩⟩ := hextract P epsilon hepsilon0 hepsilon1 S
    54	  exact htransfer P epsilon hepsilon0 hepsilon1 S w v
    55	
    56	end

     4	/-!
     5	# Pauli basis test soundness interface
     6	
     7	This module contains the quantitative error function and the closed definitions
     8	used to state Pauli basis test soundness.  The carriers are concrete
     9	finite-dimensional vectors and matrices so that the soundness proof can use the
    10	existing Hilbert-space API without introducing a dependency cycle.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	The interface supports blueprint
    15	`thm:pauli`, with paper origin
    16	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    17	The distance functionals use blueprint `def:state-distance` and
    18	`def:povm-distance`.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    22	
    23	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    24	
    25	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    26	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	noncomputable section
    29	
    30	/-- The Pauli-test error scale.  The argument order is `(a, b, ε, m, d, q)`;
    31	the powers are real `rpow`s and the asymptotic constants are absorbed into `a`,
    32	as specified by blueprint `thm:pauli`,
    33	paper `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
    34	-/
    35	noncomputable def deltaQld (a b ε : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
    36	  a * Real.rpow ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) a *
    37	    (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
    38	      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))
    39	
    40	/-- Monotonicity obligation for adjusting the universal constants in
    41	`deltaQld` on the source parameter domain. This Lean-only helper supports the
    42	enlargement of `a` and shrinkage of `b` for `0 ≤ ε ≤ 1` recorded in
    43	`rem:pauli-robustness-form` and stated as `lem:delta-qld-mono-support`,
    44	blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex`; the source makes this constant adjustment
    45	at `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1402`. It is
    46	not an additional hypothesis of `thm:pauli` or `lem:qld-4-7`. -/
    47	theorem deltaQld_mono {P : AdmissibleParams} {a a' b b' ε : ℝ}
    48	    (ha0 : 1 ≤ a) (ha : a ≤ a') (hb : b' ≤ b) (hb' : 0 < b')
    49	    (hε0 : 0 ≤ ε) (hε1 : ε ≤ 1) :
    50	    deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q ≤ deltaQld a' b' ε P.m P.d P.q := by
    51	  have hmd : (1 : ℝ) ≤ ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) : ℝ) :=
    52	    Nat.one_le_cast.mpr (Nat.mul_pos P.one_le_m P.hd)
    53	  have hmd0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) : ℝ) := by linarith
    54	  have hq : (1 : ℝ) ≤ (P.q : ℝ) := by
    55	    obtain ⟨k, -, hk⟩ := P.hq
    56	    rw [hk]
    57	    exact_mod_cast Nat.one_le_pow _ _ (by norm_num)
    58	  unfold deltaQld
    59	  simp only [Real.rpow_eq_pow]
    60	  have h1 : ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ a ≤ ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ a' :=
    61	    Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le hmd ha
    62	  have h2 : ε ^ b ≤ ε ^ b' := Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_ge' hε0 hε1 hb'.le hb
    63	  have h3 : (P.q : ℝ) ^ (-b) ≤ (P.q : ℝ) ^ (-b') :=
    64	    Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le hq (neg_le_neg hb)
    65	  have h4 : (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(b * ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) : ℝ))) ≤
    66	      (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(b' * ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) : ℝ))) :=
    67	    Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le (by norm_num)
    68	      (neg_le_neg (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hb hmd0))
    69	  have hsum : 0 ≤ ε ^ b + (P.q : ℝ) ^ (-b) +
    70	      (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(b * ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) : ℝ))) := by
    71	    have := Real.rpow_nonneg hε0 b
    72	    have := Real.rpow_nonneg (Nat.cast_nonneg P.q) (-b)
    73	    have := Real.rpow_nonneg (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2)
    74	      (-(b * ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) : ℝ)))
    75	    linarith
    76	  exact mul_le_mul (mul_le_mul ha h1 (Real.rpow_nonneg hmd0 a) (by linarith))
    77	    (add_le_add (add_le_add h2 h3) h4) hsum
    78	    (mul_nonneg (by linarith) (Real.rpow_nonneg hmd0 a'))
    79	
    80	/-- The ideal auxiliary state `aux ⊗ EPR_q^{⊗M}` in the shuffled register
    81	ordering.  The EPR factor is the concrete `eprState` from blueprint
    82	`def:EPR`; paper
    83	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`).
    84	-/
    85	noncomputable def idealState (P : AdmissibleParams)
    86	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    87	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    88	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')) :
    89	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
    90	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) ×
    91	      (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) ℂ).symm
    92	    (fun p =>
    93	      ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA' × ιB') ℂ) aux (p.1.1, p.2.1)) *
    94	        ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P) ℂ)
    95	          (eprState (PauliRegister P)) (p.1.2, p.2.2)))
    96	
    97	/-- The A-side ideal Pauli projector, with identities on the auxiliary and
    98	B-side registers.  This is a concrete matrix form of the operator comparison
    99	in blueprint `thm:pauli`; paper
   100	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
   101	-/
   102	noncomputable def pauliProjOnA'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
   103	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   104	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
   105	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
   106	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   107	  fun p q =>
   108	    if p.1.1 = q.1.1 ∧ p.2 = q.2 then
   109	      pauliProj W u p.1.2 q.1.2
   110	    else 0
   111	
   112	/-- The symmetric B-side ideal Pauli projector from blueprint
   113	`thm:pauli`, paper origin
   114	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   115	-/
   116	noncomputable def pauliProjOnB'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
   117	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   118	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
   119	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
   120	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   121	  fun p q =>
   122	    if p.1 = q.1 ∧ p.2.1 = q.2.1 then
   123	      pauliProj W u p.2.2 q.2.2
   124	    else 0
   125	
   126	/-- Lift a conjugated A-side effect to the full ideal register in blueprint
   127	`thm:pauli`, paper origin
   128	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   129	-/
   130	noncomputable def liftedAEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   131	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   132	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   133	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   134	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × PauliRegister P))
   135	    (M : Op S.ιA) :
   136	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   137	  fun p q =>
   138	    if p.2 = q.2 then
   139	      (conjIsometry φA M) p.1 q.1
   140	    else 0
   141	
   142	/-- Lift a conjugated B-side effect to the full ideal register in blueprint
   143	`thm:pauli`, paper origin
   144	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   145	-/
   146	noncomputable def liftedBEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   147	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   148	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   149	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   150	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P))
   151	    (M : Op S.ιB) :
   152	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   153	  fun p q =>
   154	    if p.1 = q.1 then
   155	      (conjIsometry φB M) p.2 q.2
   156	    else 0
   157	
   158	/-- A finite witness packaging the auxiliary dimensions, isometries, and state
   159	from `thm:pauli`.  This structure is a Lean-only encoding of the existential
   160	data in the paper theorem; it introduces no extra hypothesis.  Blueprint
   161	`thm:pauli`, paper origin
   162	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   163	-/
   164	structure PauliSoundnessWitness (P : AdmissibleParams)
   165	    (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)) where
   166	  ιA' : Type
   167	  ιB' : Type
   168	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA']
   169	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB']
   170	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA']
   171	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB']
   172	  φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   173	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × PauliRegister P)
   174	  φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   175	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P)
   176	  aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')
   177	  aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1
   178	
   179	attribute [instance] PauliSoundnessWitness.ιAFintype PauliSoundnessWitness.ιBFintype
   180	  PauliSoundnessWitness.ιADecidableEq PauliSoundnessWitness.ιBDecidableEq
   181	
   182	/-- The A-side operator-distance quantity appearing in the soundness
   183	conclusion.  It is the finite-sum realization of `def:povm-distance` from
   184	`def:povm-distance`, paper origin
   185	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`.
   186	-/
   187	noncomputable def pauliOperatorDistanceA
   188	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   189	    (w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   190	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   191	      ‖applyOperatorToState (liftedAEffect S w.φA
   192	        (((S.A (pauliQuestion P W)).postprocess pauliAnswerOrZero).effect u) -
   193	      pauliProjOnA'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   194	
   195	/-- The symmetric B-side operator-distance quantity from blueprint
   196	`def:povm-distance`, paper origin
   197	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`.
   198	-/
   199	noncomputable def pauliOperatorDistanceB
   200	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   201	    (w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   202	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   203	      ‖applyOperatorToState (liftedBEffect S w.φB
   204	        (((S.B (pauliQuestion P W)).postprocess pauliAnswerOrZero).effect u) -
   205	      pauliProjOnB'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   206	
   207	end
   208	
   209	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

  1434	\[\delta_{\qld}(\eps,m,d,q) = a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})\]
  1435	 for universal constants $a \geq 1$ and $0 < b < 1$ such that the following holds. For all admissible parameter tuples $\qldparams = (q,m,d)$ and for all strategies $\strategy = (\ket{\psi},A,B)$ for the game $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ that succeed with probability at least $1 - \eps$, there exist local isometries $\phi_\alice: \mH_\alice \to \mH_{\alice'} \otimes \mH_{\alice''},\phi_\bob: \mH_\bob \to \mH_{\bob'} \otimes \mH_{\bob''}$ (where $\ket{\psi} \in \mH_\alice \otimes \mH_\bob$ and $\mH_{\alice''},\mH_{\bob''} \cong (\C^q)^{\otimes M}$ with $M = 2^m$) and a state $\ket{\aux} \in \mH_{\alice'} \otimes \mH_{\bob'}$ such that

    16	
    17	\section{Purpose}
    18	
    19	When a formalization relies on a cited mathematical source, the cited source
    20	should remain intact.  It is a source, not an errata file.  If a possible gap,
    21	missing hypothesis, incorrect numerical constant, or other mathematical
    22	discrepancy is found, the matter should be recorded in a separate LaTeX note.
    23	In this repository such notes live under \path{docs/paper-gaps/}.  The same
    24	principle applies when the formal development has already diverged from the
    25	cited source, for instance by changing a statement so that it compiles, or by
    26	using a different mathematical route because an available formal-library theorem
    27	has a slightly different form.  Such a note is a mathematical note first, and a
    28	record of the formalization second: it should be readable by a mathematician or
    29	mathematical physicist who has not followed the issue discussion.
    30	
    31	The note should isolate the mathematical mechanism.  It should say what the
    32	cited source asserts, what the cited results actually imply, where a term or
    33	hypothesis is lost, and what statement the formal development proves instead.
    34	If the formal proof takes a different route, the note should explain the
    35	replacement argument and the hypotheses on which it rests.  This is especially
    36	important when the proof uses a theorem, construction, or convention from
    37	Mathlib which is not part of the cited argument.  In that case the note should
    38	state the Mathlib result in ordinary mathematical language, explain how it is
    39	specialized to the notation of the paper, and compare its hypotheses and
    40	conclusion with the step it replaces.  It should not merely say that \Lean{} did
    41	not accept a proof, that the modified proof compiles, or that a named library
    42	lemma was applied.
    43	
    44	The documents in this directory should themselves follow this standard.  A
    45	policy or template which reads like a checklist will tend to produce checklist
    46	notes; the examples and templates should therefore be written as mathematical
    47	prose.
    48	
    49	\section{Concision and Readability}
    50	
    51	A paper-gap note should be short enough that a reader can understand the issue
    52	in one sitting.  The first page should answer four questions: what the source
    53	uses, how hard the remaining formal work is, what the formalization or audit
    54	checked, and what the current verdict is.  Begin with a short
    55	\emph{At a glance} section when the note concerns an open or recently resolved
    56	formalization task.  That section should estimate the difficulty, the rough
    57	implementation weight, the split between Mathlib reuse and project-local work,
    58	and the key Mathlib APIs or modules.  Use honest ranges, not false precision.
    59	
    60	The \emph{Key theorem forms} section should be Section~2, immediately after
    61	\emph{At a glance}.  Put the theorem forms before the source details so the
    62	reader knows what the formalization is aiming to prove.  After that, keep the
    63	source assertion, the mechanism being checked, the blueprint/formal comparison,
    64	and the conclusion.  Use more sections only when a counterexample or long
    65	derivation genuinely needs room.
    66	
    67	Keep background to the minimum needed for the local point.  Prefer one clear
    68	special case over a general restatement of the surrounding theorem.  Use displayed
    69	equations for the source assertion, the key calculation, and the theorem forms;
    70	avoid displays for traceability data, declaration names, or long lists.  The
    71	blueprint/formal comparison should be compact and should not repeat the theorem
    72	forms.  The section ``Form of the Note'' below specifies where traceability data
    73	belongs; the body should read as mathematical prose, not as a log.
    74	
    75	If the verdict is that there is no mathematical discrepancy, say so plainly and
    76	stop.  Keep the conclusion highly compact, normally under twenty source lines.
    77	If the only remaining work is an implementation task, name it briefly and link
    78	the issue or pull request in a footnote.
    79	
    80	\section{When the Investigation Starts}
    81	
    82	The investigation starts when the obstruction appears to be mathematical rather
    83	than merely formal.  No final judgement is needed at this stage.  It is enough
    84	that, after reading the relevant source and attempting the corresponding formal
    85	statement, the proof seems to require a different scalar, an additional
    86	hypothesis, a different tensor placement, a distinction between two objects which
    87	the prose identifies, or an auxiliary assertion not supplied by the cited
    88	argument.
    89	
    90	The same investigation should also start when such a deviation is discovered
    91	after the fact.  If the existing formal development or informal blueprint has
    92	already changed the statement, strengthened a hypothesis, weakened a conclusion,
    93	inserted an unadvertised lemma, or replaced the cited proof by a different
    94	formal-library argument, the mathematical change should be documented even if all
    95	relevant files already compile.
    96	
    97	At this early stage the purpose is to preserve the question while it is still
    98	local.  The note may later conclude that the matter is only notational, that an
    99	intermediate estimate in the cited source needs a harmless correction, that a
   100	missing hypothesis is genuinely needed, or that no discrepancy remains.  Thus
   101	the trigger is not the severity of the eventual verdict, but the appearance of a
   102	real mismatch between the cited reasoning and the statement that can be
   103	formalized.
   104	
   105	A failed tactic search, a missing formal lemma, or an inconvenient coercion is
   106	not enough.  The obstruction must survive translation back into ordinary
   107	mathematics.
   108	
   109	Once a cited statement is established to be mathematically false, the repair
   110	and escalation procedure is governed by Section~6 of
   111	\path{local/protocols/issues-prs.md}.  Before asking the human owner to choose a
   112	replacement, a dedicated mathematical-gap session must produce a correction
   113	which is correct, sufficient for every paper and blueprint use, and minimal,
   114	then iterate it against the Lean statement and its downstream consumers.  A
   115	Claude Fable~5.1 session is currently launched by the owner session through its
   116	Agent tool; a Codex main session requests that lane on progress log~\#27 rather
   117	than dispatching a Codex worker.  Only after the astra poller reports
   118	availability on owner inbox~\#26 does the Codex route become
   119	\texttt{dispatch.sh --role mathfix} with astra.  A change to a mathematical
   120	definition or game is escalated immediately; other repairs reach the owner
   121	inbox only after the shared convergence budget expires.
   122	
   123	Sometimes an investigation uncovers an improvement that is not a discrepancy:
   124	the formalization works correctly, but it could be simplified by using an
   125	existing library, replacing a custom type, or adopting a cleaner proof route.
   126	These are not, by themselves, paper-gap notes.  They are action items.  When
   127	such an improvement is identified, open a GitHub issue or pull request that
   128	describes the proposed change.  If the investigation also produces a paper-gap
   129	note, link the issue or pull request from that note: the note records the
   130	mathematical justification, and the issue or pull request drives the
   131	implementation.
   132	
   133	\section{When to Write a Note}
   134	
   135	A note should be written once the source argument and the formal proof no longer
   136	match as mathematical arguments.  This includes, for instance, a numerical
   137	estimate whose constant does not follow from the cited lemma, a displayed
   138	conclusion which uses an unstated hypothesis, or a step in which two objects are
   139	identified although they must remain distinct.  In analytic, algebraic,
   140	probabilistic, or quantum arguments, such distinctions may concern the domain of
   141	a map, the placement of a tensor factor, the type of an outcome, the distinction
   142	between a structure and a substructure, or the scalar carried by an approximation
   143	relation.
   144	
   145	A note is required when an audit finds that a Lean declaration associated with a
   146	source-labelled statement has acquired an extra non-source hypothesis, such as
   147	bridge, residual, repair, producer, or obligation-structure data.  Such a
   148	declaration is temporary proof debt, not a replacement for the source theorem,
   149	and should not be introduced merely to avoid a \verb|sorry|.  The note must say
   150	plainly that the Lean result is conditional, identify the source-faithful theorem
   151	form that remains to be proved, and give the intended obligation discharger or
   152	removal plan.  The blueprint should not mark the source-labelled statement with
   153	\verb|\leanok| by pointing to this conditional helper.
   154	
   155	Changing a Lean theorem away from the statement in
   156	\path{references/ldt-paper/} is strongly discouraged.  A paper-gap note should
   157	not make such a change look routine: it should explain the mathematical
   158	necessity, or else classify the change as proof debt to be removed.
   159	
   160	When an existing conditional helper is audited, the first task is to extract any
   161	argument it already contains into source-faithful lemmas.  If the remaining
   162	bridge hypothesis cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the formal
   163	development should restore the source theorem statement and record the missing
   164	proof obligation explicitly, rather than retaining the strengthened statement as
   165	though it were the paper theorem.
   166	
   167	This requirement is not meant to classify every explicit Lean side condition as
   168	a discrepancy.  Positivity, nonemptiness, decidability, field-model instances,
   169	and denominator nonvanishing hypotheses may be faithful encodings of the domain
   170	in which the paper's theorem is stated.  The note should distinguish such
   171	boundary hypotheses from hypotheses that supply an unproved step of the paper
   172	argument.
   173	
   174	A note is also appropriate when the proof becomes formal only after changing an
   175	intermediate scalar, weakening a conclusion, strengthening a hypothesis, or
   176	inserting an additional lemma which is not simply an expansion of the cited
   177	argument.  These are mathematical changes, even when they are harmless for the
   178	final theorem.  It is likewise appropriate when an available formal-library
   179	theorem proves the needed result under a somewhat different formulation from the
   180	cited source.  In that case the note should be deliberately pedagogical.  It
   181	should explain, in ordinary mathematical language, what the replacement result
   182	says, how it is specialized, which hypotheses are new or differently packaged,
   183	and why the resulting statement is a legitimate substitute for the step in the
   184	cited argument.  If the issue remains open after reasonable attempts, the note
   185	should say what has been checked and what remains unknown.
   186	
   187	\section{Counterexamples}
   188	
   189	If the cited assertion appears to be false, the note should not stop at saying
   190	that the proof cannot be formalized.  It should give the counterexample, or the
   191	smallest relevant part of it, in ordinary mathematical notation.  The example
   192	should be accompanied by enough verification that the reader can see both sides:
   193	the hypotheses of the cited assertion hold, and its conclusion fails.
   194	
   195	When feasible, the counterexample should also be formalized in \Lean{}.  This is
   196	especially valuable when the example is finite, algebraic, computational, or
   197	otherwise small enough that the failure can be checked without reproducing the
   198	whole surrounding theory.  The note should then state the mathematical content
   199	of the checked counterexample and identify the corresponding Lean declaration in
   200	a footnote.  The Lean file is not a substitute for the prose: the prose should
   201	still explain why the example refutes the cited assertion.
   202	
   203	\section{Revision of a Note}
   204	
   205	A paper-gap note may be provisional.  It may begin as soon as the mathematical
   206	obstruction has been isolated well enough to state the question, and it may be
   207	revised as the calculation, the blueprint, or the corresponding \Lean{}
   208	declarations become clearer.  The first version need not know the final
   209	classification, but it should say plainly which mathematical point is known and
   210	which point remains unsettled.
   211	
   212	Later revisions should not make the note into a chronological log.  They should
   213	rewrite the document so that it remains a coherent account of the present
   214	mathematical understanding.  If the verdict changes, the conclusion should state
   215	the current verdict; the linked issue or pull request can preserve the earlier
   216	discussion.
   217	
   218	\section{Form of the Note}
   219	
   220	Each note should stand on its own.  It should give the date, cite the relevant
   221	source article, and provide enough traceability for the reader to locate the
   222	original passage and the project discussion.  GitHub issues and pull requests may
   223	be linked with \verb|\href|, and source files, line ranges, and labels should be
   224	recorded when they help the reader check the claim.  These references should
   225	serve the exposition rather than govern it: the main text should be organized
   226	around the mathematical assertion and its proof.
   227	
   228	The note should introduce its notation before using it.  Symbols for
   229	measurements, tensor factors, approximation relations, and error parameters
   230	should be named in prose.  If an approximation relation is state-dependent, the
   231	state should be named, or its defining expression should be given when this can
   232	be done briefly.  Only after the notation is in place should the note state the
   233	assertion in the cited source, using a bibliographic citation such as
   234	\verb|\cite[Section~...]{...}| when the section or chapter is known.
   235	
   236	Only the relevant hypotheses should be reproduced.  If the question is a scalar
   237	substitution, a missing term, or a missing hypothesis, the note should not quote
   238	a long unrelated part of the proof.  It should give the cited lemma or
   239	proposition in the special case actually used, then display the calculation or
   240	logical implication in which the discrepancy appears.

    26	      deltaQld a (b / 2) epsilon P.m P.d P.q := by
